one_line: Liquid AI's Maxime Labonne on training 350M to 24B edge models: small models have their own constraints, narrow targeting and doom-loop fixes via DPO and RL.
summary: Maxime Labonne (head of post-training at Liquid AI) argues that small edge models are not just shrunk versions of big ones. He frames them around three constraints: memory-bound, task-specific, and latency-sensitive. On architecture, he says Liquid's LFM2 uses a gated short-convolution block chosen by on-device profiling on CPU and GPU, not theory, because it was faster and used less memory than attention alternatives. On training, he reports pretraining a 350M model on 28T tokens and still seeing gains, which he says is beyond Chinchilla-style compute-optimal scaling. The talk then covers "doom looping" (repeated text that never stops) in small reasoning models, which he says SFT does not fix but DPO on on-policy data and RL with verifiable rewards plus a repetition penalty largely do. He ends by arguing small models should be paired with tools (for example web search and a Python environment for long context), since reasoning matters more than memory for them.

key_ideas.idea: Small models have three constraints (memory-bound, task-specific, latency-sensitive) and need their own design, not scaled-down big-model recipes.
key_ideas.detail: Low knowledge capacity means they should be narrow and good at a few things like summarization, extraction and tool use. The speaker says the stages are the same as for big models, but how you run them differs.

key_ideas.idea: For tiny models, the embedding layer can take a large share of parameters, so the effective reasoning size is much smaller than the headline count.
key_ideas.detail: He says Gemma 3 270M is about 63% embedding parameters and Qwen 3.5 0.8B about 29%, since big teacher vocabularies were distilled into the student. Liquid's LFM2 keeps the embedding share small so more parameters do the work.

key_ideas.idea: Architecture was chosen by profiling on the target hardware rather than on theory.
key_ideas.detail: Liquid profiled on an AMD Ryzen Max Plus CPU, a Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra, and GPU. The gated short-convolution block beat sliding-window attention, Gated DeltaNet, gated linear attention and GQA on speed and memory at the sizes they tested.

key_ideas.idea: Pretraining still helps at very small scale, well past compute-optimal token counts.
key_ideas.detail: LFM 2.5 350M was pretrained on 28T tokens. The speaker says this is more than Chinchilla would suggest and that the model still improved, so he thinks it was under-trained by the newer scaling laws he cites.

key_ideas.idea: Target a few capabilities (here data extraction and tool use) rather than being average across everything.
key_ideas.detail: The speaker says that if a small model is not best at code or math, it does not matter much for its intended users. Narrow SFT and RL data help more than broad mixes.

key_ideas.idea: Doom looping is a major small-model failure mode, and it is fixed in preference alignment and RL, not SFT.
key_ideas.detail: After mid-training the doom-loop ratio on LFM 2.5 1.2B Thinking was about 15-16%, and SFT barely changed it. DPO reduced it a lot and RL made it almost non-existent.

key_ideas.idea: Small models should be paired with tools and environments to cover their weaknesses in knowledge and long context.
key_ideas.detail: Hallucination from low knowledge capacity can be cut by giving the model web search. Long-context weakness can be worked around with a recursive language model environment where the model uses Python. He argues reasoning, not knowledge, is the key capability for tool use.

techniques.name: On-policy DPO pairs for doom-loop suppression
techniques.how: Sample 1M prompts. For each, draw five temperature-sampled rollouts from the policy being trained, plus one temperature-0 rollout that is expected to loop. An LLM jury scores all six. Highest score is chosen, lowest is rejected, so looping outputs become negatives.
techniques.when: When training a small reasoning model that loops on hard prompts and you want general preference gains as well as loop removal.

techniques.name: Repetition penalty inside RLVR
techniques.how: Use verifiable rewards (for example extracting a final answer, which gives zero reward if missing) and add a small n-gram repetition penalty. Keep temperature sampling so rollouts are diverse.
techniques.when: When RL is already in the pipeline and you want loops reduced as a side effect, without a separate fix stage.

techniques.name: Fix training stage by diagnosis
techniques.how: Watch RL reward curves. If RL does not learn, suspect missing cold-start SFT data for that task. Add similar SFT samples, then restart from the SFT stage and rerun the later stages.
techniques.when: When RL on a narrow task stalls on a small model.

techniques.name: Profile architecture on target hardware
techniques.how: Implement candidate operators on the actual phone/CPU/GPU targets and measure latency and memory before choosing a block design, instead of relying on FLOP counts.
techniques.when: When designing or choosing an architecture for on-device latency constraints.

techniques.name: Tool and environment offload for small models
techniques.how: Give the model web search for knowledge questions and a Python/recursive-LM environment for long contexts, and train it for reliable tool use.
techniques.when: When the model is too small to hold the knowledge or context a task needs but has good reasoning.

numbers.claim: Model family sizes released by Liquid, from 350M to 24B parameters, across text, vision and audio.
Gemma 3 270M: embedding layer is about 63% of total parameters.
Qwen 3.5 0.8B: embedding layer is about 29% of total parameters.
LFM2 embedding layer is much smaller than competitors'. The auto-caption says about 90%, which contradicts the point being made, so it is likely about 10%. Treat as unverified.
LFM 2.5 350M was pretrained on 28 trillion tokens, above Chinchilla compute-optimal, and still improved.
Doom-loop ratio on LFM 2.5 1.2B Thinking after mid-training across hard benchmarks: about 15-16%. After SFT it barely moved.
Doom-loop ratio after RL on LFM 2.5 1.2B Thinking is described as almost non-existent. DPO reduced it significantly, but no exact figure is given.
Qwen 3.5 0.8B in reasoning mode: over 50% doom loops on the speaker's tests.
Preference-data generation uses about 1 million prompts, with 5 temperature rollouts and 1 temperature-0 rollout per prompt.

hot_takes: Small models are not just scaled-down versions of big models and need their own training recipe.
SFT is not the right stage to fix doom loops; preference alignment and RL are.
Pretraining a 350M model on 28T tokens is still worth it, even though it is far past Chinchilla's compute-optimal point.
Competitor Qwen 3.5 0.8B in reasoning mode loops over half the time, which he says shows a shrunk big-model recipe does not work for edge models.
Small models do not need large knowledge; they need reasoning to use tools well.

relevance.why: InferCraft targets small local models on one RTX 5090. The talk is on training small models rather than serving them, but its doom-loop measurement and tool-pairing advice are relevant to a small local tier.
relevance.action: Add a doom-loop metric (share of outputs with a repeated n-gram block over a length threshold) to the L2B eval harness for any small local reasoning model.

relevance.why: ProsHarness runs long Claude Code loops. A repetition detector like the one described could catch stuck agent turns before they burn tokens.
relevance.action: Add a repeated-block detector in the loop runner that flags a turn repeating the same long n-gram and triggers checkpoint-and-stop.

relevance.why: Practical evidence that small-model failures (looping, weak long context) are fixed in post-training and by tools, plus a measured loop ratio per training stage. Relevant to the recurring interest in cheap-model (Haiku) pipelines and eval methods.
relevance.action: Measure loop rate per stage when fine-tuning or choosing a cheap model for a pipeline, and read the Liquid LFM2 technical report for the DPO and RLVR details.
